raw_response.adversarial_critique: Claude's extracted row accurately captures the trial's powered headline outcome—household use of a JMP-improved primary drinking-water source—which rose from 43% in control clusters to 83% in VEA clusters (adjusted ITT +0.33, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.45; N = 1,312 households in 121 clusters; Table 2, p. 7), alongside a +26 pp gain in improved sanitation (p. 7) and +0.64 SD gain in household water satisfaction (Table 3, p. 7). However, the single-row coding omits substantial co-primary and secondary nulls: two of the four preregistered primary outcomes—daily water collection time (-3.0 min, 95% CI -19.7 to 13.6) and daily water quantity collected (+2.3 L, 95% CI -4.2 to 8.7; Table 2, p. 7)—as well as the household financial cost of water index (+0.13 SD, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.36) and the village-level functional improved water-point index (+0.13 SD, 95% CI -0.18 to 0.44; N = 328 villages; Table 3, p. 7) were all statistically indistinguishable from zero. Subgroup regressions in Table 4 (p. 8) further reveal stark provincial heterogeneity, with completely null effects on all four primary outcomes in South Kivu (N = 468), a null water-source point estimate in Kongo Central (+0.24, 95% CI -0.06 to 0.53), a statistically significant 43-minute increase in daily water-hauling time in Kasai (95% CI 13 to 72), and a 13-litre drop in water collected in Kasai Central (95% CI -23 to -4). On scope and Family B fit, although the outcome directly measures household drinking-water access, VEA bundles participatory governance (signed Health Zone agreements, elected village WASH committees, and "Healthy Village" certification) with roughly US$2,000 for water construction and US$2,000 for sanitation construction per village (p. 4), meaning the trial cannot isolate institutional governance effects from external capital subsidies (p. 9; also note Claude's exposure text loosely says "community financing" whereas infrastructure funds came from FCDO/UNICEF grants alongside petty-cash maintenance training). Because `Improved water source` was explicitly the primary outcome used to power the trial (p. 5) and no pooled access outcome showed an adverse effect, Claude's `Favourable` direction is empirically supported, though multiplicity and bundled-treatment caveats apply.

evidence_quotes.quote: Power calculations focused on the primary outcome of whether the household uses an improved water source as their primary source of water.
In the intervention group, 83% of households reported that their primary water source was improved, compared with 43% in the control group
We found no evidence of any intervention effects on any of the primary outcomes in subgroup analyses of South Kivu province.
There is far less ability to disaggregate any distinct mechanism of action in the VEA trial than in the aforementioned studies, which separately tested water, sanitation and nutrition interventions.
